sections.h2: Where is the Cocke County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
Find it inside the Newport courthouse at 111 Court Avenue, Tennessee 37821. The counter is staffed 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays, plus Saturday mornings from 8:00 until 11:00.

Reach the office by phone at (423) 623-7540, by fax at (423) 623-7556, or by email at ccrod@cockecountytn.gov. Mark McGaha, who joined the staff in September 2010, runs it. The county legislative body appointed him in December 2016 after Linda Benson retired.

Any deed that transfers a Cocke County house has to land here before it becomes part of the record. Your closing agent usually handles the delivery, though an owner can bring the paper in person. The county's Register of Deeds page carries the staff list and fee schedule.

sections.h2: Which fees apply when a Cocke County deed gets recorded?
sections.html:
Warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, deeds of trust, leases, liens, judgments, restrictions, agreements and amendments all follow one rule: $5.00 a page, a $10.00 floor, and a $2.00 data processing charge on top.

The county's list cites Tennessee Code 8-21-1001. Other document types are priced separately:

  • A release of one lien: $10.00 for the first two pages and the $2.00 processing fee, with $5.00 more per extra page and per extra deed reference.
  • An assignment or modification: $10.00 covers one assignment on one or two pages, again with $2.00 added and $5.00 for each extra page or reference.
  • A fixture filing under the financing statement heading: $15.00, with $15.00 per additional indexed party. Spouses are indexed as two names.
  • A charter: $5.00 through five pages plus $2.00, then 50 cents a page.
  • A certified copy: $1.00 plus $1.00 for every page.

The preparer's name and address must appear on everything except releases and charters. Assignments and modifications must also recite the maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes, which can be stated as $0.

sections.h2: How much is the state transfer tax on a Cocke County sale?
sections.html:
The county page lists the state levy as $3.70 per $1,000, the same as 37 cents per $100. The Tennessee Department of Revenue describes it as a realty transfer tax on all transfers of real property, figured generally on the larger of what was paid and what the property is worth.

Take a $158,000 house: that is 1,580 units of $100 at $0.37, or $584.60. Cocke County also lists a $1.00 probate fee, collected only in cases where state tax is paid.

New debt secured by the property triggers a second levy, the indebtedness tax. The county lists $1.15 per $1,000 with the first $2,000 exempt, and the state help page gives $0.115 per $100. Both taxes trace to Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409.

sections.h2: What will register staff do, and what is off limits?
sections.html:
Clerks accept filings, index them and make copies. Drafting is another matter: the office says it may not write documents or run title searches, since its people are neither bonded nor licensed attorneys.

That line matters if you inherited the house or plan to sell without an agent. A title company or lawyer writes the deed and reviews ownership history, and the register's role starts once the instrument is signed.

The register also runs an email alert system. Enter a first and last name plus an email address on the site the county links to, and any later recording under that name triggers a message. An owner of a house they plan to sell, or of land they seldom visit, can use it to catch a forged deed early.

sections.h2: What is Cocke County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Cocke County is a rural, mountainous county on Tennessee's eastern edge. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 37,889 residents, a 5.3% rise from the 35,999 counted in April 2020.

sections.h2: Which towns and landscape shape property in Cocke County?
sections.html:
Newport anchors the county as seat and largest city. Parrottsville is the lone other incorporated town, and Cosby is a census-designated place. Of 443 square miles in total area, the Census lists 436 as land.

The Great Smoky Mountains fill the southern stretch, while Ridge-and-Valley terrain covers the north. The French Broad River crosses the northern part, with Douglas Lake formed along a portion of it, and English Mountain rises over the west. Interstate 40, US 25, US 70 and US 321 serve the county, and slices of Cherokee National Forest, the Appalachian Trail and Great Smoky Mountains National Park lie within its borders.

The General Assembly carved the county out of Greene County on October 9, 1797, and named it for Senator William Cocke. Terrain like this makes the legal description in a deed worth a careful read, so ask your closing agent to match it to the parcel before recording.

sections.h2: Who bills the property tax on a Cocke County house?
sections.html:
The state's calendar puts the assessment date at January 1, with taxes payable from the first Monday in October and delinquent after the last day of February.

The register records deeds and does not bill property tax. Phone the Cocke County Trustee for a payoff on the parcel before closing, and the Assessor of Property for the appraised value and class. Your title company will want the same numbers for the settlement statement.

Disputing a value? The Comptroller's schedule sets August 1 as the general deadline to reach the State Board of Equalization, or 45 days after the county board sends its notice, whichever is later.

sections.h2: What should you carry to the counter?
sections.html:
Bring the original signed and notarized deed, both parties' names and addresses, the preparer's name and address, and payment. Ask the office how it takes payment before you drive over.

  • The deed, with the preparer's name and address shown on it.
  • The price or value, so staff can compute the transfer tax.
  • Money covering the page charge, the $2.00 processing fee and $3.70 per $1,000 of tax.
  • For a release, the lien details and deed book reference, as each extra reference is $5.00.

An unusual document? Call (423) 623-7540 or send an email to confirm charges first.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Cocke County?
faqs.a: Expect $5.00 per page, a $10.00 minimum and a $2.00 data processing fee. A three-page warranty deed runs $15.00 plus $2.00, so $17.00 before state tax. The county website lists the full schedule.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Cocke County house sale?
faqs.a: It is $3.70 per $1,000 (37 cents per $100), generally measured on the greater of price or value. A $200,000 sale owes $740. The county lists it as state tax, and the Department of Revenue cites Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409.

faqs.q: Can the Cocke County register prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office says it may not prepare documents or perform title searches, because staff are neither bonded nor licensed attorneys. Ask a title company or attorney to write the deed; the register then records it.

faqs.q: Is the Cocke County Register of Deeds open on Saturday?
faqs.a: Yes, Saturday mornings from 8:00 to 11:00. Weekday hours run 8:00 to 4:30. Call (423) 623-7540 or visit 111 Court Avenue in Newport.

faqs.q: How do I find out whether anyone recorded a deed in my name?
faqs.a: Sign up for the register's email alert on the site the county links to. You give your name and an email address, and every later recording under that name sends you a message. You can also call the office about a specific filing.
